position: Office of the Secretary, Compliance for Grants and Other Federal Funding
proposal: The Mandate says FEMA and other DHS grants should go only to recipients that certify compliance with federal immigration law, including honoring detainers, and that they are registered with and use E-Verify (for states and localities, across all of government). State and local recipients would also commit to full information sharing with federal law enforcement and immigration authorities, including motor vehicle and voter registration databases. The text exempts post-disaster funding (and, as worded, nonhumanitarian funding) from these preconditions.

Data-sharing conditions covering motor vehicle and voter registration databases.

status_summary: EO 14159 (signed 2025-01-20, section 17) told the Attorney General and DHS to seek to stop federal funds going to jurisdictions that obstruct immigration enforcement, and EO 14287 (signed 2025-04-28) told agencies to identify funds to such jurisdictions for suspension or termination; DHS revised its standard grant terms on 2025-03-27 and 2025-04-18 to require state and local recipients to certify cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, including information sharing. On 2025-09-24 the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (Illinois v. FEMA, No. 1:25-cv-00206) vacated those conditions and permanently enjoined their enforcement against the plaintiff states (20 states and the District of Columbia), on 2025-10-14 also vacated the award articles on compliance with federal immigration law and barred materially similar terms against them, and the government dismissed its appeal on 2026-09-16, per the states' later motion. FEMA applied FY2026 immigration conditions, including a detainer cooperation term, to nine grant programs by a bulletin of 2026-09-18, and on 2026-10-07 the plaintiff states asked the court to enforce its orders against them, citing nearly 1 billion dollars at risk, while a separate suit by other states over the FY2026 conditions (No. 26-cv-485) is pending. No requirement tied to E-Verify use or to motor vehicle and voter database access was found.

timeline.event: EO 14159 section 17 directed the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to seek lawful steps to stop federal funds reaching jurisdictions that obstruct immigration enforcement.
DHS revised its standard grant terms to require state and local recipients to certify cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, including joint operations and information sharing.

DHS FY 2025 Standard Terms and Conditions, Version 3 (dated 2025-04-18), require in section C.IX that recipients comply with the information-sharing and other immigration statutes, honor cooperation requests including joint operations and short-term detention under a valid detainer, give access to detainees and not publicize enforcement operations, and certify compliance under penalty of perjury, with the same certification required of subrecipients and contractors; no E-Verify term appears.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (via CourtListener RECAP)

timeline.event: EO 14287 directed publication of a list of sanctuary jurisdictions and had agencies identify federal funds to them for suspension or termination.
Twenty states sued FEMA and DHS in the District of Rhode Island over the immigration conditions (Illinois v. FEMA, No. 1:25-cv-00206).

The District of Rhode Island (Illinois v. FEMA, ECF 71) grants the plaintiff states summary judgment and denies the government's cross-motion, declaring the contested DHS immigration conditions (six terms in the standard terms plus a certification that recipients will not operate programs benefiting illegal immigration) arbitrary and capricious and contrary to the Spending Clause, vacating them and permanently enjoining their enforcement against the plaintiff states only; it orders briefing within 14 days on whether that relief is complete and does not reach the statutory authority argument.

The court (ECF 75) finds that award documents added the conditions to take effect if the injunction were stayed or vacated, vacates the conditions and the award articles titled Compliance with Federal Immigration Law, permanently enjoins enforcement of them and of any materially similar term against the plaintiff states and their instrumentalities and subdivisions, and orders award documents amended and reissued within seven days without the trigger language.

FEMA Information Bulletin No. 538 notifies the 21 plaintiff states in Illinois v. FEMA (counting the District of Columbia) that FY2025 awards under six programs are amended to rescind the cooperation terms and the immigration-compliance articles, implementing the 2025-10-14 order; FEMA says it will confirm the amendments in each award file once the funding lapse ends.

title: Condition FEMA and DHS grants on immigration compliance, E-Verify and data sharing
uncertainties: The FY2025 DHS Standard Terms and Conditions Version 3 (footer dated 2025-04-18) were opened as exhibit 59-2 on storage.courtlistener.com, and FEMA Information Bulletin No. 538 (2025-10-21) was opened on a copy posted by caloes.ca.gov (neither on a dhs.gov or fema.gov host, so both are copies); a Vermont state posting of the FY2026 DHS standard terms was also opened. The 2025-03-27 revision date and the March 2025 wording still rest on a trade publication, and the FY2026 conditions and FEMA Information Bulletin No. 582 are described only in the states' motion, a party filing, and by an external retrieval; Bulletin No. 582 itself was not opened. The court orders of 2025-09-24 (ECF 71) and 2025-10-14 (ECF 75) were opened and read on CourtListener copies. The September order defines the contested conditions as six immigration-related terms in the DHS standard terms plus a separate certification, seven items in all, which corrects earlier record wording of six. The appeal dismissal date of 2026-09-16 comes only from the states' motion and an external retrieval citing a litigation tracker; the appeal docket was not opened. No ruling on the 2026-10-07 motion was found, and the judge assigned to it was not identified. Relief covers only the plaintiff states; whether the conditions are operative for other states was not confirmed beyond the pending separate suit. No Federal Register notice of the grant conditions was found. The Mandate's E-Verify and database-access certifications are broader than the cooperation conditions found. Stage is a judgment call: blocked reflects the vacatur and injunction for the plaintiff states and the dropped appeal, while the FY2026 terms show DHS continuing to issue similar conditions. Points read in the opened copies (latest check, 2026-10-22): the FY2025 exhibit's Communication and Cooperation section requires compliance with the information-sharing statutes, compliance with other immigration laws, honoring cooperation requests including joint operations and short-term detention under a valid detainer, access to detainees, and no disclosure of enforcement operations, with a certification under penalty of perjury that recipients must obtain from subrecipients and contractors, and a materiality clause; E-Verify is not mentioned in it, which fits the record's finding that no E-Verify term was found. Bulletin No. 538 notifies 21 plaintiff states that FEMA is amending FY2025 awards under six programs to rescind the cooperation terms and the immigration-compliance articles, implementing the 2025-10-14 order; this fits the record's count of 20 states plus the District of Columbia. The posting on hsu.vermont.gov is a section titled as the DHS Standard Terms and Conditions for FY 2026 awards, with a printed effective date of 2026-04-16 and a statement that it revises the 2025-04-18 version; whether that is the date DHS released the terms was not confirmed. It keeps the information-sharing and certification terms, does not mention E-Verify, and says DHS may analyze and tailor the conditions by program; it is not used for a dated event. An external retrieval additionally reports that Bulletin No. 582 (2026-09-18) applies the FY2026 term to listed programs for awards on or after 2026-08-28 and not to others; this is unverified. Court text and court status are unchanged from the 2026-10-22 court-record pass.
